subject: ventures/open-tennis-robots
professional: a sports-ballistics engineer who designs two-wheel ball launchers, paired with an embedded/machine-safety engineer (IEC 60204-1 and ISO 13850 e-stop practice, MicroPython firmware review). The first would check that the flight model lands where it says and that wheel speeds follow from the launcher geometry; the second would check first whether the watchdog and e-stop actually hold under every input and over long uptime, and whether reset can restart the machine without a deliberate local action.

evidence.completeness: Unchanged in scope since 2026-11-08. CLI subcommands run end to end here: aim (three targets above), drill drill.example.json (compiles, first shot elev 21.24 az -6.52), collect --balls 60 --practice (distance 97.9 m, 1 dump trip), catch-study (above); unreachable targets fail loudly ('target (30.0, 0.0) is out of reach at 15.0 m/s', and I confirmed by a sweep that 15 m/s tops out at 17.9 m of carry, so the refusal is genuine). Browser port: node --test '*.test.mjs' 21/21 pass. Live page now loads: curl https://marisstella.app/open-tennis-robots/ -> 200, title 'Open Tennis Robots ...' (the 2026-11-08 audit could not load it). Firmware controller, protocol, collector and feeder manufacturing packages and BOMs present. Still openly not done (README roadmap 2-9): feeder actuator brackets, azimuth drive, netting trough; no bench test; no measured return distribution. The four commits since the last audit (#14079, #14308, #14379, #14409) each add one ~25-line statics/tolerance check to cad/otr_cad/params.py with a test and a blog post; none touches the defects the last audit listed.
evidence.verification: Ran: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q tests` -> 38 passed; `node --test '*.test.mjs'` -> 21 pass; `cd cad && PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q tests` -> 16 passed, 20 skipped, 1 FAILED (test_take_up_parts_match_the_design imports otr_cad.feeder, which needs build123d, without the skipUnless(HAVE_CAD) guard the other CAD-solid tests carry; CI installs build123d so it only breaks local runs). Seeded mutations, each reverted with git checkout and git status clean afterwards: (M1) ballistics.lift_coeff 2.0 -> 2.6: all 38 Python tests pass, BUT the CI step 'Fixtures are current' (`python -m tennisbots.fixtures; git diff --exit-code fixtures/`) shows reference.json changed (26 lines) and sim.test.mjs then fails 2 of 5, so CI catches it; the 2026-11-08 audit reported this mutation as surviving because it ran the unit tests only. (M2) bounce spin sign flip `s - du/(alpha*r)` -> `s + du/(alpha*r)`: 38 pass; fixture regeneration changes 2 lines, so CI's fixture gate catches it, unit tests do not. (M3) catcher.py:37 net half-width `net_width/2` -> `net_width` (prior audit's high defect): 38 pass AND fixtures unchanged: survives everything, still. (M4) controller.py:96 drop the base speed clamp: 38 pass, survives. (M5) controller.py:111 disable physical e-stop sensing: caught (test_physical_estop_latches fails). Score 2: the fixture gate is a real regression net for the flight model, but the catch-rate headline, a firmware safety clamp, and the hardware layer (main.py: feed interlock, timing) remain untested, and the prior audit's top defect is unfixed.
evidence.craft: Read ballistics.py, launcher.py, firmware/esp32/controller.py and main.py, the new params.py methods (launch_window, plate_clearance, axle_squaring, track_tie) and their tests. Python side is clean: typed, units and frames documented, RK4, bracketing+bisection aim, firmware logic testable on CPython via `hw`. Score drops from 3 to 2 because of a defect a senior embedded/MicroPython reviewer would reject on sight, not found in the last audit: main.py:259/262 passes raw time.ticks_ms() into Controller.tick, and controller.py:114 (watchdog) and :121 (telemetry) use plain subtraction, though main.py:260 itself uses ticks_diff for dt. MicroPython ticks_ms wraps (period 2**30 ms, about 12.4 days, on the ESP32 port; from recollection of the MicroPython docs, not fetched). Ran scratchpad wrap.py: controller created and last heartbeat at 2**30-100, Pi silent, then ticks 2**30-1, 50, 400, 5000, 60000 -> watchdog_tripped stays False and telemetry_bytes stays 0 at every step. So after ~12 days of uptime telemetry stops for good, and a Pi that dies within 300 ms of the wrap never trips the watchdog; main.py:182 (`now >= gate_open_until + 400`) has the same wrap. Other defects, carried over: controller.py:96 forwards the SET_BASE target unclamped (wrap.py: SET_BASE(30000 mm, 99999 mm/s) -> hw.set_base(30000, 3000)); launcher.py:123 aim exits after 6 azimuth passes without signalling non-convergence (in my probes with +-3000 rpm sidespin it did converge, miss 0.000 m); unguarded CAD test; params.py is now an 840-line pair of dataclasses with 76 methods, the CAD statics accreting one method per session.
evidence.claims: Backed: catch table (two more cells reproduced), BOM totals, 'no simulated return cleared a 2.5 m frame' (too high 0%), ITF constants, no-warranty text (index.html:173, README, safety.md), usage.mjs wired on the page (index.html:180), honest 'no robot has been built yet' (README:53, llms.txt). Not backed, all carried over from 2026-11-08 and unfixed: hardware/safety.md:25-26 'Command limits in firmware: wheel rpm, aim angles, base speed and drive speed are clamped whatever the Pi sends' is literally true for base speed, but the base position target is not clamped or rail-limited anywhere (controller.py:96, main.py:137), which a reader of 'Command limits' reasonably takes as covered; README:66 and llms.txt advertise 'firmware with watchdog' while the watchdog is not wrap-safe (above). (200, a redirect page) instead of marisstella.app.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through as a builder: I can plan shots (aim/drill give angles and wheel rpm that an independent integrator reproduces), size a net (catch-study), price a build (BOM), and fabricate the collector from its package. I cannot yet trust the feeder to run near a person: base target unclamped, e-stop clear is a software command from the Pi, watchdog not wrap-safe, feed interlock untested, launcher efficiencies (0.85/0.5) and the return distribution are unvalidated guesses on which the headline 91% rests, and feeder CAD still omits actuator brackets, azimuth drive and netting. The last four sessions spent the flagship's effort on second-order feeder tolerances (plate yaw 4.7x margin, track tie factor 104) rather than the safety defects or the bench test that the roadmap itself puts first. A tinkerer can start; a builder cannot finish a safe feeder from it.
evidence.domain: Physics: compared against the sports-ballistics method the code cites: constant C_d 0.55, C_L = 1/(2 + v/(r w)), friction-limited bounce with COR 0.75 and I = 0.55 m r^2 (Cross's tennis-ball value; a thin shell would be 2/3), two-wheel exit speed = efficiency x mean surface speed, spin from the surface-speed difference. I re-derived the bounce impulse/torque signs and the launcher kinematics and they are right; departures (no Reynolds dependence of C_d, no in-flight spin decay, one court surface) are stated. The new CAD statics are standard first-order engineering (small-angle tolerance stack with worst-case and RSS, rigid two-tie statics with a couple F*e/span, Coulomb nip traction from squeeze stiffness) with every input flagged as an assumption to measure. Machine safety departs from practice: per IEC 60204-1/ISO 13850 resetting an e-stop must not itself enable restart and should be a deliberate local action; here the contactor coil is simply in series with the mushroom switch (hardware/electronics.md:19-23), so releasing the button re-powers the motor bus at once, and the only further gate is a CLEAR_ESTOP the Pi can send without a human; there is no monitored contactor or safety relay. Physics alone would be a 3-4; the safety method keeps it at 3 at most.

defects.what: Firmware watchdog and telemetry use plain subtraction on raw time.ticks_ms() values, which wrap (2**30 ms on ESP32 MicroPython). Simulated: after a wrap with the Pi silent, watchdog_tripped stays False and no telemetry is ever sent again; the feed gate timing at main.py:182 has the same bug. main.py:260 already uses ticks_diff for dt, so the fix is known in-file.
Still unfixed from 2026-11-08: doubling the catch-net half-width passes all 38 Python tests, the 21 JS tests and the fixture gate; nothing pins a catch rate or the README's catch table.

Still unfixed: SET_BASE target forwarded unclamped (30000 mm passes through), no rail limit in firmware, and removing the base speed clamp is not caught by any test; safety.md's 'Command limits in firmware' reads as covering the base.

Still unfixed: e-stop reset is the mushroom switch in series with the contactor coil plus a software CLEAR_ESTOP from the Pi; no deliberate local reset, no monitored contactor (IEC 60204-1 / ISO 13850 practice).
Still unfixed: feed interlock and all hardware-layer timing live in main.py with no tests.

(The auditor also listed llms.txt's github.io link; the build rewrites it and the served llms.txt points at marisstella.app, so that part is dropped: portfolio/quality/README.md, 'Judge what is served'.)
CAD param test imports otr_cad.feeder (needs build123d) without the skipUnless(HAVE_CAD) guard, so the documented local test run fails without the CAD toolchain.
aim() still leaves its azimuth loop after 6 passes without raising if not converged (converged in every case I probed).

verdict: The numbers are right: an independent integrator reproduced three aimed shots to 1e-4 m, three bounces matched the rigid-body impulse equations by hand, wheel rpm, the new CAD launch window, plate-yaw and axle tolerance stack all recompute exactly, and two more catch-table cells and both BOM totals match the README. The 2026-11-08 audit undercounted one safeguard (CI's fixture gate does catch flight-model mutations), but none of its defects were fixed: the net-width mutation still passes everything, the base target is still unclamped and the e-stop still clears from software. This audit adds a new safety-relevant firmware bug: the watchdog and telemetry are not wrap-safe on MicroPython ticks. Since the last audit the four sessions on this flagship each added a small feeder-tolerance calculation rather than these fixes. It does not meet the bar (verification, claims below 3; median 2): a sound design study, not yet something a machine-safety engineer would sign off to run beside a player.
